l: the travelers' threatened execution, Sky Island, THE ARRIVAL OF POLYCHROME
s: Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill are threatened with being thrown over the edge of the Pink Country because Tourmaline claims they do not harmonize with its color scheme. Polychrome prevents the execution by invoking the Pink Country protection law and then makes Trot Queen.

l: the arrival of Polychrome, Sky Island, THE ARRIVAL OF POLYCHROME
s: Polychrome arrives when the Rainbow descends near Trot, Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, Tourmaline, and the Pinkies. She leaves the Rainbow to help the travelers, overturns their threatened execution, and changes the rule of the Pink Country by installing Trot as Queen.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: Trot is made Queen of the Pink Country after Polychrome rescues her, and the Pinkies enthusiastically accept her as their ruler. Polychrome departs on the Rainbow after promising to watch over Button-Bright, while Rosalie the Witch pledges to protect and advise Trot. Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill decide that they must recover Button-Bright's Magic Umbrella from the Boolooroo in the Blue Country so they can return home. Rosalie proposes raising an army from the Pink Country, marching through the Fog Bank, and forcing the Boolooroo to surrender the umbrella.

l: Trot, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: Trot becomes the new Queen of the Pink Country and is dressed in one of its plain pink gowns. She greets the Pinkies, enjoys their enthusiastic homage, and initially feels proud of her new position, but she agrees that recovering the Magic Umbrella and returning home may be preferable. She approves the plan to prepare for an expedition against the Boolooroo.

l: Polychrome, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: Polychrome helps establish Trot as Queen by leading her before the Pinkies and then departs with her sisters on the Rainbow. She asks Rosalie the Witch to protect Trot and promises Button-Bright that she will keep watch over him.

l: Button-Bright, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: Button-Bright witnesses Trot's coronation and agrees that returning to Earth is preferable to remaining in the Pink Country. He explains that the Boolooroo has the Magic Umbrella and says that the Royal Record Book proves the Boolooroo has already reigned for his lawful three hundred years.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: Cap'n Bill questions whether Trot can remain Queen for long because the Pinkies expect their Queen to live poorly and without amusement. He supports recovering the Magic Umbrella, argues that the Pinkies can defeat the Blueskins, and urges Trot to undertake the campaign against the Boolooroo.

l: Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: Rosalie pledges to serve and protect Trot while she rules the Pink Country. She proposes using the Pinkies as an army to march through the Fog Bank, conquer the Boolooroo, and recover the Magic Umbrella, and she says she can greatly assist the expedition.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: The Pinkies enthusiastically accept Trot as their new Queen, kneel before her, and kiss her hand. They are described as a great nation pledged to obey her commands and possessing sharp sticks, and they are expected to provide the army for the planned campaign.

l: the Pink Country, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: The Pink Country receives Trot as its new Queen after Tourmaline is relieved of the position. Its customs require the Queen to wear a poor, plain dress and to live without much pleasure.

l: the Boolooroo, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: The Boolooroo is in possession of Button-Bright's Magic Umbrella and is expected to resist giving it up. The Royal Record Book reportedly proves that he has already completed his lawful three-hundred-year reign, making Ghip-Ghisizzle a possible successor.

l: Magic Umbrella, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: The Magic Umbrella has been stolen by the Boolooroo. Button-Bright, Trot, and Cap'n Bill believe that recovering it is their means of flying safely home to Earth.

l: the Blue Country, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: The Blue Country is where the Boolooroo and the Blueskins live. The planned route to it leads through the Fog Bank.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: The Blueskins are described as larger than the Pinkies but as cowards. Their weapons are winding-up cords with weights on the ends, in contrast to the Pinkies' sharp sticks.

l: the Rainbow, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: The Rainbow appears over the Court of the Statues and carries Polychrome and her dancing sisters away into the sky. Its colors then fade and the arch dissolves, while Polychrome says that behind the clouds is always the Rainbow.

l: the Queen's rule, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: Trot is uncertain how she will rule the Pink Country and asks the people to enjoy a holiday while she considers it. She learns that the Pinkies expect their Queen to be poor and without fun, making the position potentially tiresome.

l: Trot's coronation, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: Trot's coronation takes place when Polychrome leads her before the assembled Pinkies. The people are impressed by Trot's friendship with Polychrome and Rosalie's humble deference, and they kneel to her and kiss her hand.

l: the planned campaign against the Boolooroo, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: Trot, Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, and Rosalie plan to enter the Blue Country, recover the Magic Umbrella, and possibly replace the Boolooroo with Ghip-Ghisizzle without fighting. They nevertheless intend to proceed prepared for a struggle and expect to begin after assembling the army in two or three days.

l: Army of Conquest, Sky Island, MAYRE, QUEEN OF THE PINK COUNTRY
s: Rosalie proposes assembling an army from the Pinkies and marching it through the Fog Bank against the Boolooroo. The army is expected to be ready in two or three days, and Cap'n Bill believes its sharp sticks will give it an advantage over the Blueskins' weapons.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: The Pinkies agree to join an expedition through the Fog Bank to fight the Blueskins, with Cap'n Bill as commander. Rosalie the Witch arranges for the King of the Giant Frogs and the giant frogs to help transport the army across the Fog Bank. The Army of Conquest reaches the Blue Country, where the Pinkies prepare to march on the Blue City after Blueskins flee toward it. Cap'n Bill believes the Pinkies can conquer the Blueskins and plans to ask them to surrender.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: The Pinkies eagerly agree to undertake the war because their lives have been monotonous and uninteresting. They form an army of two hundred warriors, travel across the Fog Bank on giant frogs, and enter the Blue Country.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: The Blueskins are described as tall, lanky, ugly, and fierce. They fight with long cords weighted at the ends, and several Blueskins flee toward the Blue City when the Pinkies arrive.

l: Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: Rosalie the Witch advises that the Army of Conquest consist of one hundred Sunsets and one hundred Sunrises. She speaks with the King of the Giant Frogs and arranges for the frogs to help the Pinkies cross the Fog Bank.

l: Army of Conquest, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: The Army of Conquest consists of one hundred Sunset warriors and one hundred Sunrise warriors, equally divided between men and women. It is placed under Cap'n Bill's command and reaches the Blue Country after riding across the Fog Bank on giant frogs.

l: Fog Bank, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: The Fog Bank is crossed by the Pinkies with the help of the giant frogs. The journey is completed in about a dozen jumps, after which the army reaches the edge of the Blue Country.

l: King of the Giant Frogs, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: The King of the Giant Frogs agrees to help Rosalie the Witch and the Pinkies pass through the Fog Bank. He carries Trot, her parrot, Rosalie, Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, and the two army captains, slowing at the edge so they can dismount comfortably.

l: giant frogs, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: The giant frogs form a barrier across the Fog Bank and carry the Pinkies on their backs. They leap together across the fog, transporting the army to the Blue Country.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: Cap'n Bill is named Commander in Chief of the expedition and explains the Fog Bank and the Blueskins' weapons to the Pinkies. He leads the army across the Fog Bank, forms it into a line of battle, and proposes marching on the Blue City to request the Blueskins' surrender.

l: the Blue Country, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: The Blue Country lies beyond the Fog Bank and has blue fields where the Pinkies land after their ride. Once there, the Pinkies remove their raincoats and prepare for battle.

l: Blue City, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: Several Blueskins rush toward the Blue City when the Pinkies arrive. Cap'n Bill intends to march the Pinkies to the Blue City and ask the Blueskins to surrender.

l: war between the Pinkies and Blueskins, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: The Pinkies agree to fight the Blueskins, believing they are braver and better armed. The conflict begins with the Pinkies entering the Blue Country and preparing to march against the Blueskins.

l: expedition through the Fog Bank, Sky Island, THE WAR OF THE PINKS AND BLUES
s: The expedition is organized as an Army of Conquest led by Cap'n Bill. With help from the King of the Giant Frogs and the giant frogs, the expedition crosses the Fog Bank and arrives safely in the Blue Country.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: The Boolooroo learns that the Book of Records is missing and prepares to have Ghip-Ghisizzle patched with Tiggle, but a Pinkie invasion interrupts the operation. Cap'n Bill's army reaches the City and forces the Blueskins to defend it while the Boolooroo closes the gates. The Six Snubnosed Princesses free Ghip-Ghisizzle from the Room of the Great Knife, but they imprison him elsewhere until he agrees to marry one of them.

l: the Boolooroo, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: The Boolooroo suspects Ghip-Ghisizzle of stealing the Book of Records and orders him bound. He plans to have Ghip-Ghisizzle patched, but abandons the operation temporarily when the Pinkies invade and orders the City gates closed.

l: Ghip-Ghisizzle, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: Ghip-Ghisizzle denies stealing the Book of Records and secretly suspects that Button-Bright took it. He is bound and scheduled to be patched with Tiggle, but the Six Snubnosed Princesses rescue him and imprison him until he agrees to marry one of them.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: The Pinkies break through the Fog Bank and march toward the City in a great army. They cause the Boolooroo to halt the patching operation and prepare the Blueskins for defense.

l: the Blue Country, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: The Blue Country is threatened by the Pinkies after they break through the Fog Bank. Its Blueskins become fearful and blame the Boolooroo's cruel treatment of the Earth people for bringing about the invasion.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: The Blueskins prepare to defend the City from the Pinkies with weighted cords. Many of them resent the Boolooroo and believe his treatment of the Earth people caused the invasion.

l: Royal Record Book, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: The Book of Records is discovered to be missing from the Treasure Chamber. Its loss frightens the Boolooroo because it may expose his fraud on the people.

l: Fog Bank, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: The Pinkies break through the Fog Bank and enter the Blue Country. Ghip-Ghisizzle fears that Button-Bright, who escaped into it, may never be seen again.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: Cap'n Bill had been ordered to mix the royal nectar at the time of his capture. His army later reaches the wall of the City but cannot enter immediately because the gates are closed.

l: the Great Knife, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: The Great Knife is prepared for the patching of Ghip-Ghisizzle and Tiggle. The Boolooroo expects the operation to make the two prisoners look ridiculous when their halves are joined.

l: the Room of the Great Knife, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: Ghip-Ghisizzle and Tiggle are bound and locked in the Room of the Great Knife while the Boolooroo deals with the Pinkie invasion. The Six Snubnosed Princesses unlock the room and remove Ghip-Ghisizzle, leaving Tiggle behind.

l: Blue City, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: The Pinkies march toward the City, prompting the Boolooroo to close and lock all its gates. Cap'n Bill's army reaches the City wall but must halt until it can find a way inside.

l: the Six Snubnosed Princesses, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: The Six Snubnosed Princesses quarrel over which of them will marry Ghip-Ghisizzle and become Queen. They free him from the Room of the Great Knife, then lock him in a vacant room until he chooses one of them.

l: Pinkie invasion, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: The Pinkie invasion interrupts the Boolooroo's attempt to have Ghip-Ghisizzle patched. It causes the City to shut its gates and forces the Blueskins to prepare for battle.

l: patching, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: Patching is the operation by which prisoners are sliced in two with the Great Knife and their halves are joined to other prisoners. Ghip-Ghisizzle is scheduled to be patched with Tiggle, but the operation does not occur before the Princesses rescue him.

l: Army of Conquest, Sky Island, GHIP-GHISIZZLE HAS A BAD TIME
s: Cap'n Bill's army reaches the wall of the City after the Pinkies break through the Fog Bank. It is forced to halt outside because the City gates are closed and locked.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: Cap'n Bill leads the Pinkies in an attack against the Blueskins, but he is captured after pursuing the fleeing Blueskins alone. Rosalie the Witch enchants the Pinkies' weapons, allowing them to defeat the Blueskins' longer lances, but her magic cannot be used again for three days. Trot, Button-Bright, and Rosalie make a rope ladder, and Rosalie gives Trot a magic ring that makes her invisible. Trot uses the ladder and ring to enter the Blue City secretly in search of Cap'n Bill.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: Cap'n Bill commands the Pinkies during the Blueskins' attack and directs them to resist with their sharp sticks. After the enchanted weapons defeat the Blueskins, he pursues them alone, falls when his wooden leg enters a hole, and is captured and bound by the Blueskins.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: The Pinkies encamp before the principal gate of the Blue City and successfully repel the Blueskins' first attack. Rosalie enchants their sharp sticks, enabling them to destroy the Blueskins' longer lances, but they fail to rescue Cap'n Bill after his capture and become despondent.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: The Blueskins first attack the Pinkies with cord-and-weights but retreat when the Pinkies use their sharp sticks. Armed with longer bluewood lances, they are defeated by the enchanted Pinkies' weapons, then capture Cap'n Bill after he falls and carry him into the Blue City.

l: the Boolooroo, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: The Boolooroo is nervous about the Pinkies and orders the Blueskins to attack them. He flees back to the City during the first attack, orders longer sharp sticks to be made, and later stops fleeing to command that the fallen Cap'n Bill be captured.

l: Trot, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: Trot worries over Cap'n Bill after his capture and asks Rosalie for a way to enter the Blue City. Wearing Rosalie's magic ring, she climbs the rope ladder, descends inside the City, and begins searching for Cap'n Bill while invisible.

l: Button-Bright, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: Button-Bright mourns Cap'n Bill's capture and is told to stay outside to lead the army and seek a way to rescue Trot and Rosalie. Trot gives him her polly before climbing the wall, and he promises to do his best.

l: Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: Rosalie sees through a vision what is happening inside the Blue City and enchants the Pinkies' sharp sticks. Because she can use only one magic charm every three days, she cannot immediately rescue Cap'n Bill, but she makes a rope ladder and gives Trot an invisibility ring to aid the rescue.

l: Blue City, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: The Blue City is enclosed by a wall and gate, and the Blueskins lock themselves inside it after the Pinkies arrive. The Blueskins capture Cap'n Bill within the City, which Trot secretly enters by climbing over its wall.

l: Rosalie's magic charm, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: Rosalie explains that she is allowed to work only one magic charm every three days. She uses the available charm to enchant the Pinkies' weapons, leaving her unable to use another charm immediately to rescue Cap'n Bill.

l: the enchanted Pinkies' weapons, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: The enchanted Pinkies' sharp sticks whirl in swift circles when the Blueskins attack. They deflect the Blueskins' longer lances, breaking them or sending them through the air and causing the Blueskins to flee.

l: rope ladder (Trot's ladder), Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: Rosalie knots ropes into a ladder long enough to reach the top of the Blue City wall. After seven attempts, she catches it on a broken flagstaff, allowing Trot to climb up and then descend into the City.

l: ring of Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: Rosalie's magic ring makes its wearer invisible to Blueskins, Pinkies, and Earth people. Trot wears it to enter the Blue City unseen, but Rosalie warns that touching another person would make Trot visible and that the ring must be returned.

l: the capture of Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: Cap'n Bill is captured after he pursues the retreating Blueskins alone and falls when his wooden leg steps into a hole. The Blueskins seize him, carry him into the Blue City, and bind him while the Pinkies are unable to reach him.

l: the Blueskins' attack on the Pinkies, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: The Blueskins' first attack fails when the Pinkies form a line with their sharp sticks and drive them back. During a second attack, the Blueskins' longer lances are destroyed or thrown aside by the enchanted weapons, causing another retreat.

l: Trot's secret entry into the Blue City, Sky Island, THE CAPTURE OF CAP'N BILL
s: Trot enters the Blue City at night by climbing Rosalie's rope ladder over the wall and descending on the inner side. Invisible because of Rosalie's magic ring, she passes a guard and hurries through the streets to search for Cap'n Bill.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: Trot enters the Boolooroo's palace at night to search for Cap'n Bill, who is being held for patching. She frees Tiggle from the Room of the Great Knife so the Boolooroo will have no one to patch Cap'n Bill to. Trot then accidentally enables Ghip-Ghisizzle to escape through a window and across the palace and City walls. Ghip-Ghisizzle reaches the Pinkies' camp, where Captain Coralie captures him and takes him to Rosalie the Witch.

l: Trot, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: Trot goes to the palace at night to find Cap'n Bill. She frees Tiggle by distracting the guard, then searches for Cap'n Bill and unknowingly helps Ghip-Ghisizzle escape when she enters his room.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: Most of the Blueskins are asleep while a few soldiers guard the palace and pursue Ghip-Ghisizzle. They search for Ghip-Ghisizzle after seeing him run along the walls, but abandon the chase when he reaches the direction of the Pinkies' camp.

l: Blue City, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: The City is quiet and blue-lit at night, with guards and residents joining the pursuit of Ghip-Ghisizzle. Its wall connects with the wall around the palace gardens.

l: the Boolooroo, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: The Boolooroo keeps Cap'n Bill hidden until morning so he can be patched to Tiggle. He has ordered the patching to take place after breakfast and has soldiers guarding the palace.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: Cap'n Bill is an important prisoner hidden by the Boolooroo. He is scheduled to be patched to Tiggle in the morning.

l: Tiggle, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: Tiggle is bound in the Room of the Great Knife, but Trot frees him. He promises to hide in a house where the Boolooroo's soldiers cannot find him, leaving the Boolooroo without the intended mate for Cap'n Bill.

l: Ghip-Ghisizzle, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: Ghip-Ghisizzle escapes from the Room of the Great Knife and is hidden in a chamber by the Six Snubnosed Princesses. When Trot enters, he escapes through the window, runs along the palace and City walls, and reaches the Pinkies' camp, where Captain Coralie captures him.

l: the Royal Palace, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: The palace is guarded at night, but Trot enters through the doorway while the guards are distracted. It contains the Room of the Great Knife, Cap'n Bill's hidden prison location, and the chamber from which Ghip-Ghisizzle escapes.

l: patching, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: The patching is scheduled for the following morning after breakfast. The Boolooroo intends to patch Cap'n Bill to Tiggle because Ghip-Ghisizzle has escaped.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: The Pinkies are camped outside the City and are treated by Ghip-Ghisizzle as preferable to his own people and their feared Boolooroo. Their forces take Ghip-Ghisizzle prisoner after he reaches their camp.

l: the Pinkies' camp, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: The Pinkies' camp lies outside the City near the City wall. Ghip-Ghisizzle leaps toward it for protection, and Captain Coralie captures him there.

l: Ghip-Ghisizzle's flight from the City, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: Ghip-Ghisizzle escapes through a window, runs along the palace garden wall and the City wall, and leaps into the field outside the City near the Pinkies' camp. The Blueskins pursue him but stop when he reaches the Pinkies.

l: being patched, Sky Island, TROT'S INVISIBLE ADVENTURE
s: Being patched involves splitting people in two with the Great Knife and joining them into a strange combination. Jimfred and Fredjim say it did not hurt as much as expected, but left them confused until they became accustomed to it.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: Trot uses the ring of Rosalie the Witch to enter the Boolooroo's apartments unseen and free Cap'n Bill, but Cap'n Bill is recaptured while trying to escape over the Blue City's wall. Trot fails to find the Magic Umbrella and remains in the palace after Cap'n Bill is taken back. Button-Bright gives Ghip-Ghisizzle the Royal Record Book, which proves that the Boolooroo's rule has unlawfully continued past its permitted term. Ghip-Ghisizzle, Rosalie the Witch, Button-Bright, and the Pinkies hold a council of war and plan to take the Blue City and capture the Boolooroo.

l: Trot, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: Trot enters the palace unseen, causes the Six Snubnosed Princesses to fight, and searches for Cap'n Bill and the Magic Umbrella. She frees Cap'n Bill and helps him reach the wall, but watches as the Blueskins recapture him. Trot stays behind in the palace to continue searching for the Magic Umbrella.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: Cap'n Bill is found asleep and bound in the Boolooroo's private apartments, with his toe tied to the Boolooroo's toe. Trot frees him, and he tries to escape by climbing from a window and crossing the City wall, but the Blueskins catch and bind him again.

l: the Boolooroo, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: The Boolooroo sleeps while Cap'n Bill is held in the adjoining room, and he has devised a cord arrangement to be awakened if the sailor tries to escape. The Royal Record Book shows that he has ruled the Blue Country beyond the lawful term and has no right to rule.

l: Ghip-Ghisizzle, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: Ghip-Ghisizzle learns from the Royal Record Book that he has been the rightful Ruler of the Blues since Thursday. He plans to force the Boolooroo to resign and agrees to let Button-Bright and the Pinkies recover the Magic Umbrella and return home if they help him.

l: Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: Rosalie the Witch previously lent Trot the ring that makes her invisible. She awaits Button-Bright, Coralie, and the others at her tent, where they hold a council of war.

l: Button-Bright, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: Button-Bright sees Cap'n Bill escaping along the wall and alerts Coralie and the Pinkies, but they arrive too late to prevent his capture. He gives Ghip-Ghisizzle the Royal Record Book and asks that the Magic Umbrella be returned so they can fly home.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: The Pinkies march toward the Blue City wall to assist Cap'n Bill's escape after Button-Bright alerts Coralie. They arrive too late and return to camp after the Blueskins recapture him.

l: Army of Conquest, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: The Pink Army is offered as a force that will fight for Ghip-Ghisizzle against the Boolooroo. Its support is conditional on Ghip-Ghisizzle returning the Magic Umbrella and allowing the adventurers to fly home.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: The Blueskins awaken when a soldier sees Cap'n Bill crossing the wall. They pursue him, use Trot's rope ladder to head him off, recapture him, and carry him back into the Blue City.

l: Blue City, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: The Blue City begins waking as Cap'n Bill attempts to escape, and its soldiers pursue him along the wall. The Blue City is the intended target of Ghip-Ghisizzle's planned attack.

l: the Blue Country, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: The Royal Record Book shows that the Boolooroo had already ruled the Blue Country for three hundred years by the previous Thursday. Ghip-Ghisizzle claims the right to rule the Blue Country and plans to replace him.

l: Royal Record Book, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: Button-Bright has kept the Royal Record Book since taking it from the Boolooroo's Treasure Chamber. Ghip-Ghisizzle reads it and discovers that the Boolooroo's lawful reign ended on Thursday, giving Ghip-Ghisizzle evidence against him.

l: Magic Umbrella, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: The Magic Umbrella is no longer beneath the cabinet in the Boolooroo's apartments when Trot searches for it. Ghip-Ghisizzle promises to return it to Button-Bright and the others if they help him take the Blue City.

l: ring of Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: The ring of Rosalie the Witch makes Trot invisible unless she touches a living creature. Contact with the blue dog, the blue lamb, or Cap'n Bill makes her visible while the contact lasts.

l: Cap'n Bill's capture, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: Cap'n Bill is captured after the Blueskins overtake him on the top of the Blue City's wall. They bind him again and carry him down into the City, disappointing Trot, Button-Bright, Coralie, and the Pinkies.

l: Cap'n Bill's escape attempt, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: Trot helps Cap'n Bill escape from the Boolooroo's apartments by lowering him from a window on a sheet and directing him to a rope ladder. He crosses the wall but cannot outrun the Blueskins, who head him off and recapture him.

l: council of war, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: Ghip-Ghisizzle, Rosalie the Witch, Button-Bright, and the others hold a council of war in Rosalie's tent after Cap'n Bill's recapture. They discuss how to take the Blue City and capture the Boolooroo.

l: being patched, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: The Boolooroo intends to patch Cap'n Bill after breakfast, pairing him with Tiggle. Trot says that Tiggle has been set free and is hiding, so the Boolooroo may need to find someone else.

l: the Boolooroo's unlawful rule, Sky Island, THE GIRL AND THE BOOLOOROO
s: The Royal Record Book states that the Boolooroo had already completed three hundred years of rule by Thursday and therefore no longer had the right to govern. He has continued ruling and has also tried to have Ghip-Ghisizzle patched to prevent him from becoming Boolooroo.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, THE AMAZING CONQUEST OF THE BLUES
s: The Boolooroo recaptures Cap'n Bill and takes him to the Room of the Great Knife to be patched. When Tiggle cannot be found, the Boolooroo orders the first living creature encountered to be brought in, and the soldiers bring a billygoat. Invisible Trot uses a rope to pull Cap'n Bill's frame away from the falling Great Knife, while the billygoat attacks the Boolooroo, soldiers, and Six Snubnosed Princesses. Trot and Cap'n Bill then bind the Boolooroo in the frame beneath the Great Knife, leaving him threatened with the punishment he intended for Cap'n Bill.

l: the Boolooroo, Sky Island, THE AMAZING CONQUEST OF THE BLUES
s: The Boolooroo discovers that Cap'n Bill has escaped, recaptures him, and orders him to be patched. After Tiggle cannot be found, he orders the first living creature encountered to be patched to Cap'n Bill, laughs at the prospect of joining Cap'n Bill to a billygoat, and tries to operate the Great Knife. The billygoat knocks him among the benches, and Trot and Cap'n Bill later tie him into the frame beneath the knife.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, THE AMAZING CONQUEST OF THE BLUES
s: Cap'n Bill is recaptured and brought to the Room of the Great Knife to be patched. Trot repeatedly pulls his frame away as the Great Knife falls, saving him, and the billygoat's attack helps clear the room. After Trot frees him, Cap'n Bill helps seize and bind the Boolooroo.

l: Trot, Sky Island, THE AMAZING CONQUEST OF THE BLUES
s: Trot remains invisible while following Cap'n Bill to the Room of the Great Knife and searches for a way to save him. She finds a rope, uses it to drag Cap'n Bill's frame away from the falling Great Knife twice, ties the billygoat to a pillar, and frees Cap'n Bill. She then helps him bind the Boolooroo beneath the knife and suggests that they can run the Blue Country themselves.

l: the Six Snubnosed Princesses, Sky Island, THE AMAZING CONQUEST OF THE BLUES
s: The Six Snubnosed Princesses enter the Room of the Great Knife in magnificent clothing to watch Cap'n Bill be patched. The billygoat attacks them, overturning their chairs and sending them tangled into the corridor in terror.

l: the Blue Country, Sky Island, THE AMAZING CONQUEST OF THE BLUES
s: The Blue Country is ruled by the Boolooroo, who says that everyone in the country hates him. After Trot and Cap'n Bill overpower him, Trot says that she and Cap'n Bill may be able to run the Blue Country themselves.

l: the Room of the Great Knife, Sky Island, THE AMAZING CONQUEST OF THE BLUES
s: The Room of the Great Knife is a large chamber with spectator benches, a royal platform, and a cutting machine used to patch prisoners. Cap'n Bill is brought there for punishment, but the billygoat's attack drives out the soldiers and royal family, leaving Trot, Cap'n Bill, and the injured Boolooroo inside.

l: the Great Knife, Sky Island, THE AMAZING CONQUEST OF THE BLUES
s: The Great Knife is a huge blade mounted in a framework reaching to the ceiling. When the Boolooroo pulls its cord, it drops to cut in two the person secured beneath it, but Trot pulls Cap'n Bill's frame away twice so that the blade strikes only the air.

l: the billygoat, Sky Island, THE AMAZING CONQUEST OF THE BLUES
s: The soldiers bring in a great blue billygoat as the first living creature they encounter. It attacks the Boolooroo, soldiers, and Six Snubnosed Princesses, clearing the Room of the Great Knife, and Trot later ties it by the horns to a doorway pillar.

l: patching, Sky Island, THE AMAZING CONQUEST OF THE BLUES
s: Patching is the Boolooroo's punishment of cutting a person in two with the Great Knife, sometimes with the stated intention of joining that person to another creature. The Boolooroo intends to patch Cap'n Bill to the billygoat, but Trot prevents it and instead helps place the Boolooroo in the frame for the same punishment.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: Trot removes Rosalie's ring and declares herself Queen of the Pinkies and Boss of the Blues, with Cap'n Bill as her General and manager. She forces the Captain of the Guards and the soldiers to obey her, has the Six Snubnosed Princesses locked in their rooms, and leaves the Boolooroo bound under the goat's guard. Trot and Cap'n Bill search the palace for the Magic Umbrella but do not find it. When told that the Pinkies are preparing to attack the City, Trot orders the Blue City to welcome them and hold a grand celebration.

l: Trot, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: Trot takes off Rosalie's ring and declares herself Queen of the Pinkies and Boss of the Blues. She makes the soldiers obey her, orders the Six Snubnosed Princesses locked in their rooms, and appoints Cap'n Bill as her General of the Army and Royal Manager of the Blue Country. She searches for the Magic Umbrella and orders the Blueskins to welcome the Pinkies with music, dancing, eating, and a grand celebration.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: Cap'n Bill supports Trot's control of the kingdom and is named her General of the Army and Royal Manager of the Blue Country. He helps Trot search the palace for the Magic Umbrella and suggests using the goat as a guard for the Boolooroo.

l: the Boolooroo, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: The Boolooroo is bound in the place where Cap'n Bill had been and is threatened with being sliced if anyone enters without Trot's permission. After Trot takes control, he remains locked in the Room of the Great Knife with the goat guarding him.

l: the Captain of the Guards, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: The Captain of the Guards returns with his soldiers after Trot threatens the Boolooroo. He chooses to obey Trot, escorts the Six Snubnosed Princesses to their rooms, guards the palace, and reports that the Pinkies are preparing to attack the City.

l: the Six Snubnosed Princesses, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: The Six Snubnosed Princesses object to Trot's rule and each claims the right to rule the kingdom. Trot has them seized and locked in their rooms under guard, after which they become meek and mild.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: The soldiers return cautiously after recovering their courage. They obey Trot rather than the princesses, lock the princesses in their rooms, and are ordered to help prepare the Blue City for the Pinkies' arrival.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: The Blueskins are described as hating the Six Snubnosed Princesses. Under Trot's orders, they are to stop quarreling with the Pinkies and welcome them to the Blue City.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: The Pinkies are enemies of the Blueskins and are preparing to attack the City. Trot declares herself their queen and orders the Blueskins to welcome their army instead of fighting it.

l: the Blue Country, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: The Blue Country comes under Trot's intended rule, with Cap'n Bill appointed its Royal Manager. Trot plans to end its conflict with the Pinkies and hold a celebration in the Blue City.

l: Magic Umbrella, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: The Magic Umbrella remains missing. Trot and Cap'n Bill search every room of the palace, including the rooms of the Six Snubnosed Princesses, but do not find it.

l: the billygoat, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: The goat is released in the Room of the Great Knife and locked inside with the Boolooroo. Cap'n Bill considers it an effective guard because everyone is afraid of it.

l: the Pinkies' attack on the City, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: The Captain of the Guards reports that the Pinkies are preparing to attack the City. Trot responds by ordering the City to open its gates and welcome them rather than resist them.

l: the grand celebration, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: Trot orders a grand celebration for the Pinkies' arrival in the Blue City. It is to include music, dancing, eating, and royal neckties to drink, with the bands, soldiers, and people taking part.

l: Trot and Cap'n Bill's rule of the kingdom, Sky Island, THE RULER OF SKY ISLAND
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill take control of the kingdom after the Boolooroo is overthrown. Trot claims authority over both the Pinkies and the Blues, while Cap'n Bill is made her General of the Army and Royal Manager of the Blue Country.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: Trot celebrates the end of the war after conquering the Blue Country and becoming Queen of Sky Island. The Pinkies and Blueskins enter the Blue City peacefully, where they feast and celebrate for three days. Trot makes Ghip-Ghisizzle the new Boolooroo, sends the former Boolooroo and the Six Snubnosed Princesses away, and orders the Great Knife destroyed. Trot, Cap'n Bill, Button-Bright, Rosalie the Witch, and their companions plan to return home once Button-Bright's umbrella is found.

l: Trot, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: Trot is welcomed by the Blueskins and becomes Queen of Sky Island, including the Pink and Blue Countries. She appoints Ghip-Ghisizzle as Boolooroo of the Blues, refuses to permit further patching, banishes the former Boolooroo and the Six Snubnosed Princesses from the palace, and orders the Great Knife destroyed.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: Cap'n Bill leads the procession with Trot and is warmly welcomed by the Pinkies and Blueskins after his escape. He supports Trot's decisions and agrees that the billygoat is braver than the entire Blue Army.

l: Button-Bright, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: Button-Bright arrives with the Pinkies and is astonished to find Trot and Cap'n Bill standing safely before the Blues. He tells the parrot to stop its long verse because he cannot hear himself think.

l: Ghip-Ghisizzle, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: Ghip-Ghisizzle explains that the Book of Royal Records proves the Boolooroo has ruled beyond his lawful three hundred years, making Ghip-Ghisizzle the lawful Boolooroo since the previous Thursday. Trot appoints him Boolooroo of the Blues, and he agrees to destroy the Great Knife, care for the billygoat, and govern the Blueskins.

l: Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: Rosalie the Witch arrives with the Pinkies, congratulates Trot, and receives her magic ring back from her. She suggests that the group return to their own country soon because conflict might arise between the Pinkies and Blueskins.

l: the Boolooroo, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The former Boolooroo is removed from the Room of the Great Knife and told that he is no longer ruler. He loses the palace and its treasure, must leave with the Six Snubnosed Princesses, and says he will reform and live as a model private citizen.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The Pinkies arrive intending to rescue Trot and Cap'n Bill and conquer the Boolooroo, but they are instead welcomed by Trot and the Blueskins. They celebrate in the Blue City but refuse to dance with the Blues and quarrel with them during the ball.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The Blueskins rejoice that the war is over and that the wicked Boolooroo has been defeated. They welcome Trot and the Pinkies, celebrate the destruction of the Great Knife, and receive Ghip-Ghisizzle as their new Boolooroo.

l: the Six Snubnosed Princesses, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The Six Snubnosed Princesses are expelled from the palace with their father and mother after Trot's victory. They are escorted by soldiers to Ghip-Ghisizzle's small cabin, screaming and suffering hysterics over the decree.

l: the Blue Country, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The Blue Country becomes part of Trot's kingdom after the conquest. Ghip-Ghisizzle is appointed its Boolooroo, while the former ruling family is removed from power.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: Trot declares herself Queen of all Sky Island except the Fog Bank. The Pink and Blue Countries remain under separate rulers while Trot retains overall sovereignty.

l: Fog Bank, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The Fog Bank remains outside Trot's kingdom. Trot and her companions plan to dive into it when they leave for the Land of Sunrise and Sunset.

l: the Royal Palace, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The palace hosts the royal feast, Trot's account of her adventures, and a grand ball for important Pinkies and Blueskins. After the conquest, its treasure and authority pass to Ghip-Ghisizzle, while the former Boolooroo and his family are expelled.

l: the Room of the Great Knife, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The Room of the Great Knife is cleared after the former Boolooroo is removed. Its frames are split, its benches are chopped into kindling, and the room's terrible furnishings are destroyed so it can be turned into a skating rink.

l: the Great Knife, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The Great Knife is broken into pieces and burned with the other furnishings from the Room of the Great Knife. Its destruction is celebrated by the Blueskins because it had caused them great unhappiness.

l: Royal Record Book, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The Book of Royal Records is recovered from the Treasure Chamber by Ghip-Ghisizzle. It reveals that the Boolooroo has reigned longer than the permitted three hundred years and establishes Ghip-Ghisizzle's lawful succession.

l: Magic Umbrella, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: Button-Bright's umbrella has not yet been found. Trot says that she and her companions will fly home as soon as they locate it.

l: the parrot, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The parrot celebrates the peaceful meeting of the Pinkies and Blueskins by shouting verses, barking like a dog, and later flying to Trot's shoulder. It sits on the back of Trot's chair during the feast, where she feeds it.

l: the billygoat, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The billygoat helps Trot defeat the Boolooroo and is treated as a hero by the Blueskins. Ghip-Ghisizzle promises to give it a fenced yard with blue grass and other food and to have the people honor it for life.

l: war between the Pinkies and Blueskins, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The war ends with the defeat of the Boolooroo and the peaceful reception of the Pinkies by the Blueskins. Trot declares that everyone must become sociable and happy rather than continue fighting.

l: the amazing conquest of the Blues, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The conquest of the Blue Country is achieved by Trot with help from the billygoat. It makes Trot Queen of the Blues and leads to Ghip-Ghisizzle becoming Boolooroo.

l: the grand feast, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The grand feast takes place in the palace after the Pinkies and Blueskins enter the City together. Trot, Cap'n Bill, Button-Bright, Rosalie the Witch, Captain Coralie, and Ghip-Ghisizzle dine in the Royal Banquet Hall with service from a hundred servants.

l: the destruction of the Great Knife, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The destruction of the Great Knife is ordered by Trot and carried out after the former Boolooroo is removed. The Knife, frames, and benches are broken up and burned while the Blueskins dance and sing in celebration.

l: patching, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: Trot forbids any more patching in the Blue Country, rejecting Ghip-Ghisizzle's request to patch the Six Snubnosed Princesses and the former Boolooroo. She decides that exile and loss of status are sufficient punishments.

l: the Boolooroo's lawful succession, Sky Island, TROT CELEBRATES THE VICTORY
s: The Book of Royal Records establishes that the former Boolooroo is no longer lawful because he has ruled beyond three hundred years. Ghip-Ghisizzle therefore becomes the lawful Boolooroo of the Blue Country, though Trot remains Queen of Sky Island.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill search the palace and surrounding area for the missing Magic Umbrella but learn that Indigo knows nothing about it. Tiggle recalls throwing an umbrella-like object onto a rubbish heap, where Cap'n Bill uncovers the Magic Umbrella and its attached equipment. Trot decides not to return home immediately because she must arrange matters in Sky Island, including helping the Pinkies return home safely and establishing a new queen for them. The Pinkies then depart the Blue City with Trot, Cap'n Bill, Button-Bright, Rosalie, and their companions.

l: Magic Umbrella, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: The Magic Umbrella is searched for throughout the palace and surrounding areas. Tiggle remembers finding it beneath a cabinet and throwing it onto a rubbish heap, where Cap'n Bill uncovers it; Button-Bright takes hold of it. Trot says it can now take them home whenever they please.

l: Trot, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: Trot helps lead the search for the Magic Umbrella and questions the palace servants. After the umbrella is found, she refuses to leave immediately because she must fulfill her duties as Queen of Sky Island, including arranging for the Pinkies to return home safely.

l: Button-Bright, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: Button-Bright searches for the Magic Umbrella and questions the former Boolooroo about it. He eagerly recognizes Tiggle's description, celebrates when the umbrella is found, and carries it during the departure from the Blue City.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: Cap'n Bill searches the palace and questions the former Boolooroo about the Magic Umbrella. He uncovers the lunch basket, seats, and umbrella in the rubbish heap, then removes and carries the seats while Button-Bright carries the umbrella.

l: Ghip-Ghisizzle, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: Ghip-Ghisizzle refuses to marry Indigo in exchange for information about the Magic Umbrella because he considers the former Princesses to have wicked hearts and evil thoughts. As the new Boolooroo, he is left in charge of the Blue Country while Trot is away.

l: Tiggle, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: Tiggle, a former servant of the old Boolooroo, had escaped and hidden in the cellar of a deserted house. After hearing that the new Boolooroo wanted him, he returns and recalls throwing the umbrella onto a rubbish heap in an alley behind the palace.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: The Pinkies helped Trot and her companions conquer the Blues and are anxious to return home. Trot arranges to escort them safely and leads them out of the Blue City toward the Fog Bank.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: The Blues are ruled by Ghip-Ghisizzle after Trot's conquest. The people are secretly glad when Trot, the Pinkies, and the other strangers leave, and they remain sullen during the departure.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: Sky Island is the realm over which Trot is Queen. Before returning home, Trot says she must straighten out affairs there, including ensuring that the Pinkies have a new queen.

l: the Royal Palace, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: The palace is searched carefully for the Magic Umbrella, but no trace is found there. Tiggle later identifies the umbrella as something he had swept from the King's rooms and discarded behind the palace.

l: search for the Magic Umbrella, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: The search begins throughout the palace with the help of many people and the palace's full liberty. After Indigo's false claim is exposed, Trot questions the servants and learns that Tiggle may know what happened to the umbrella.

l: the amazing conquest of the Blues, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: Trot's conquest of the Blues results in Ghip-Ghisizzle becoming Boolooroo of the Blue Country. Trot orders him to rule kindly and avoid making trouble while she is away.

l: departure of the Pinkies, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: The Pinkies depart from the Blue City with Coralie and Captain Tintint forming their ranks and the Pinkie Band playing a march. They leave through the blue-barred gateway and travel across the country toward the Fog Bank.

l: return of Trot and her companions to Earth, Sky Island, THE FATE OF THE MAGIC UMBRELLA
s: The recovered Magic Umbrella makes it possible for Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill to return home whenever they wish. Trot postpones the return until she has fulfilled her duties in Sky Island and helped the Pinkies get home.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: Trot, Button-Bright, Rosalie the Witch, Cap'n Bill, and the Pinkies enter the Fog Bank to reach the Pink Country with the help of the frogs. The Frog King refuses to let them pass while Button-Bright carries his umbrella, but the umbrella transforms into a huge elephant and frightens the frogs away. The elephant leads the travelers through the fog and changes back into the Magic Umbrella at the edge of the Pink Country.

l: Trot, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: Trot enters the Fog Bank with Button-Bright, Rosalie the Witch, Cap'n Bill, and the Pinkies. She argues that the umbrella must accompany them and follows the transformed elephant through the fog to the Pink Country.

l: Button-Bright, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: Button-Bright carries his Magic Umbrella and holds it over himself and Trot. He drops it when it begins transforming, then follows the elephant and later picks up the umbrella after it returns to its original form.

l: Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: Rosalie the Witch signals for the frogs to help the travelers cross the Fog Bank. She cannot make the frogs allow the umbrella through and says that the fairies controlling it must be very powerful.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: Cap'n Bill travels through the Fog Bank with the others and carefully minds his wooden leg. He becomes so excited and frightened by the events that he mumbles strange sentences.

l: King of the Giant Frogs, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: The Frog King refuses to let the travelers pass while Button-Bright carries the umbrella, calling it insulting to his dominions. When the umbrella becomes an elephant and charges, he flees before the other frogs.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: The Pinkies put on raincoats before entering the Fog Bank and follow the elephant through it. By the time they near the Pink Country, they are dripping wet and their legs are tired and aching.

l: giant frogs, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: The frogs appear to help carry the travelers across the Fog Bank, but they refuse to advance with the umbrella present. They flee and hide in the moist banks when the umbrella transforms into a huge elephant.

l: Fog Bank, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: The Fog Bank is crossed by the travelers with the frogs' assistance and later under the guidance of the transformed elephant. Its pink glow signals that the Pink Country is near.

l: the Pink Country, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: The Pink Country is the travelers' destination beyond the Fog Bank. The group reaches its edge after following the elephant through the fog.

l: Magic Umbrella, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: The Magic Umbrella is rejected by the Frog King as an insult to the foggy climate. It transforms into a huge elephant, leads the travelers through the Fog Bank, and returns to its umbrella form at the edge of the Pink Country.

l: elephant (the Magic Umbrella), Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: The elephant grows from the Magic Umbrella after its carved head's eyes glow, its trunk sways, and the umbrella swells. It charges the frogs, leads the travelers through the fog, and then shrinks back into the umbrella.

l: umbrella's transformation into an elephant, Sky Island, THE ELEPHANT'S HEAD COMES TO LIFE
s: The umbrella's transformation into an elephant begins when it trembles, shakes, and sends red sparks from the carved elephant head's eyes. After Button-Bright drops it, it becomes a complete elephant of monstrous size and later changes back into the Magic Umbrella.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, TROT REGULATES THE PINKIES
s: Trot and her companions return with the Pinkies to the Pink Country, where the people welcome them. Tourmaline refuses to become Queen again, so Trot creates a new law granting the Queen the same food, clothing, housing, money, and leisure as everyone else, but no more. Trot appoints Rosalie the Witch as Queen of the Pinkies and orders a new palace and statues for Rosalie, Tourmaline, and herself. The Pinkies give Trot the royal band and jewel, and she announces that she and her companions will soon fly back to Earth.

l: Trot, Sky Island, TROT REGULATES THE PINKIES
s: Trot returns to the Pink Country with her companions and becomes its Queen temporarily. She creates a new law giving the Queen equal conditions with the people, appoints Rosalie the Witch as Queen, orders a new palace and statues, and prepares to return to Earth.

l: Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island, TROT REGULATES THE PINKIES
s: Rosalie the Witch refuses to become Queen while the old law would make the ruler poor and miserable. After Trot changes the law, Trot appoints Rosalie Queen of the Pinkies because she is sensible, loved, respected, and able to use her powers to protect the people.

l: Tourmaline, Sky Island, TROT REGULATES THE PINKIES
s: Tourmaline arrives dressed in fine robes and earnestly refuses Trot's offer to make her Queen again, explaining that she is enjoying freedom from the poverty and hardships of the position. Trot orders a pink statue of Tourmaline to be placed in the Court of the Statues.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, TROT REGULATES THE PINKIES
s: The Pinkies joyfully welcome Trot and her companions back to their land and accept the new law as just. They accept Rosalie as Queen, agree to build her a new palace and erect statues, and give Trot the royal band of pink gold with its pink jewel.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, TROT REGULATES THE PINKIES
s: Trot identifies herself as the Queen of Sky Island when announcing that she will leave Rosalie to rule the Pink Country while she returns to Earth.

l: the Pink Country, Sky Island, TROT REGULATES THE PINKIES
s: The Pink Country welcomes Trot and her companions after their return from the Blue Country. Trot leaves Rosalie the Witch to rule it under the new law.

l: Poverty Queen, Sky Island, TROT REGULATES THE PINKIES
s: Trot has the Royal Scribbler record a law stating that the Queen shall have the same food, dresses, good times, housing, and spending money as the people, but no more than her share. If the Queen seeks more than her share, the law provides that she will be taken to the edge and pushed off.

l: Queen of the Pink Country, Sky Island, TROT REGULATES THE PINKIES
s: Under the new law, the Queen of the Pinkies will no longer be required to endure poverty and hardship, but will receive the same conditions as the people and no more. Trot first holds the position temporarily and then appoints Rosalie the Witch to it.

l: return of Trot and her companions to Earth, Sky Island, TROT REGULATES THE PINKIES
s: Trot announces that she and her friends will leave the Pink Country and return to Earth. She tells the Pinkies that they may gather after dinner to watch the group fly away through the sky.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright leave Sky Island in the Magic Umbrella and travel through the sky toward Earth. They pass clouds, a Rainbow with Polychrome and the Daughters of the Rainbow, stars, and a huge bird before landing near Trot's house. Trot returns home to her mother, while Button-Bright stays overnight and then flies to Philadelphia. Several days later, Trot learns that Button-Bright arrived safely and that his father locked the Magic Umbrella in an attic chest.

l: Trot, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: Trot gives the parrot to Rosalie, says goodbye to the Pinkies, and travels home with Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright in the Magic Umbrella. She reaches Trot's house, greets her mother, and later receives Button-Bright's postal card.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: Cap'n Bill prepares the seats and lunch basket, pilots the return trip, and helps Trot and Button-Bright travel from Sky Island to Earth. He says that getting home again was the best part of the adventure.

l: Button-Bright, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: Button-Bright checks the Magic Umbrella before the departure and travels with Trot and Cap'n Bill to Earth. He stays overnight at Trot's house, then flies to Philadelphia and later writes that he arrived home safely.

l: Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: Rosalie accepts the parrot from Trot and says goodbye when Trot leaves. She believes that she, Coralie, and Tourmaline will remain on Sky Island because they have no Magic Umbrella.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: After the Pinkies are dismissed, they reunite in the Court of the Statues with their Pink Band to see Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright depart. They play music and throw kisses as the travelers disappear.

l: Magic Umbrella, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: The Magic Umbrella carries Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright from Sky Island to Earth after being commanded to take them to Trot's house. Button-Bright later uses it to fly to Philadelphia, and his father locks it in a strong chest in the attic.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: Sky Island is where Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright say goodbye to Rosalie, Coralie, Tourmaline, the Pinkies, and the Pink Band. They leave it by flying upward in the Magic Umbrella.

l: Earth, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: The travelers eventually see Earth below them and fly over the ocean before reaching the mainland. The Magic Umbrella carries them to the high bluff near Trot's house.

l: Trot's house, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: Trot's house is a white cottage near the giant acacia on the high bluff. Trot returns there at dusk and finds her mother busy in the kitchen.

l: the journey home, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: The journey home takes Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright from Sky Island through the clouds and open sky to Earth. They encounter a Rainbow, stars, and a huge bird, eat food from the lunch basket, and land safely near Trot's house.

l: flight from Sky Island to Earth, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: The flight begins when the Magic Umbrella obeys the instruction to take the travelers to Trot's house on Earth. It moves through clouds and clear sky, passes near Polychrome and the Daughters of the Rainbow, and ends with a gentle landing on a high bluff.

l: Button-Bright's return home, Sky Island, THE JOURNEY HOME
s: Button-Bright remains at Trot's house overnight and leaves early the next morning for Philadelphia using the Magic Umbrella. Several days later, he reports that he reached home safely and that his father locked the umbrella away.

l: Little Wizard Stories of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: In the Emerald City, the Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger leave the Throne Room intending to frighten people by tearing apart a person and eating a fat baby. They encounter a lost baby and its injured mother, but instead comfort and rescue them. The mother thanks the beasts and says they have never had an evil thought, which shames them. The Lion and Tiger conclude that it is better to be cowardly or hungry than to do wrong or be cruel.

l: Emerald City, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: The Emerald City is the center of the fairy Land of Oz and contains the palace where Princess Ozma rules. The Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger leave the palace and walk through its quiet streets before returning.

l: Throne Room, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: The Throne Room is where Princess Ozma listens to the troubles of her people for an hour each day. The Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger serve as guardians there, although they usually have nothing to do except look fierce and remain quiet.

l: Princess Ozma, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: Princess Ozma is the Ruler of Oz and sits on a throne of glistening emeralds in the Throne Room. The Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger are her chief guardians.

l: Cowardly Lion, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: The Cowardly Lion complains that his guarding job is unimportant and imagines tearing a person to pieces to make people fear him. When he meets the baby's mother injured and unable to walk, he gently carries her home instead. He later says that being a coward is better than doing wrong.

l: Hungry Tiger, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: The Hungry Tiger says that he longs to eat fat babies and joins the Cowardly Lion in leaving the palace to prove their power. When he finds the lost baby, he comforts and carries the child instead of eating it. He later admits that it is better to go hungry than to be cruel to a little child.

l: Ozma's chief guardians, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: The Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger are Ozma's chief guardians. They are more ornamental than useful because the people of Oz are seldom naughty and no one disturbs Princess Ozma's audiences.

l: lost baby, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: The lost baby sits in the middle of a street crying because the baby has lost its mother. The Hungry Tiger comforts and carries the baby safely back to its mother, and the baby kisses the Tiger's nose.

l: baby's mother, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: The baby's mother rushes out to rescue the lost baby, trips over her skirt, and injures herself. The Cowardly Lion carries her home while the Hungry Tiger carries the baby, and she thanks them for helping her.

l: fat babies, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: The Hungry Tiger claims to be hungry for fat babies and imagines that eating one would make people fear him. When he encounters a real baby, he cannot bring himself to eat the child and instead protects it.

l: hunger, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: The Hungry Tiger repeatedly complains of hunger, especially for fat babies. After choosing not to eat the lost baby, he remains hungry but decides that going hungry is better than being cruel.

l: cowardice, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: The Cowardly Lion openly identifies himself as cowardly and imagines attacking someone only to flee before anyone can punish him. After helping the baby's mother, he concludes that cowardice is preferable to doing wrong.

l: cruelty, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, THE COWARDLY LION AND THE HUNGRY TIGER
s: Cruelty is rejected by both beasts when they choose to help the lost baby and the injured mother instead of harming them. The Hungry Tiger specifically concludes that it is better to remain hungry than to be cruel to a child.

l: Little Wizard Stories of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: Dorothy and Toto travel through the wild wooded hills at the southeast of Oz and meet a tiny ferryman who claims he can carry them across a black-water lake. The ferryman becomes the giant Crinklink, carries them to Crinklink's log castle, and orders Dorothy to wash a huge pile of dishes. While Dorothy works, Toto attacks the sleeping Crinklink, who is revealed to be the Wizard of Oz in disguise. The Wizard explains that he staged the danger to teach Dorothy not to travel alone through the Land of Oz, and Dorothy decides to return to the Emerald City of Oz.

l: Dorothy, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: Dorothy travels with Toto through the wild wooded hills at the southeast of Oz despite the Wizard of Oz's warnings. She is captured by the disguised Wizard, ordered to wash dishes, and frightened into believing Crinklink may harm her. After learning that the adventure was a lesson, she is angry at being fooled and decides to return to the Emerald City of Oz.

l: Toto, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: Toto accompanies Dorothy and understands everything she says, although he cannot talk. He growls at the ferryman and Crinklink, becomes frightened when Crinklink carries him and Dorothy away, and later attacks the sleeping Crinklink to save Dorothy. The attack helps reveal that Crinklink is actually the Wizard of Oz.

l: Wizard of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: The Wizard of Oz disguises himself as the ferryman and Crinklink to prove that it is dangerous for Dorothy to travel alone in a fairy country. He frightens Dorothy with a false threat, then reveals himself after Toto attacks him. He releases the animal button creatures and takes Dorothy back toward the Emerald City of Oz.

l: Crinklink, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: Crinklink is presented as a terrifying giant who carries Dorothy and Toto across the black-water lake and takes them to his log castle. He threatens Dorothy with punishment and orders her to wash his dishes, but he is ultimately revealed not to exist. The supposed Crinklink was the Wizard of Oz in disguise.

l: Land of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: The Land of Oz contains magical places and creatures, including the wild wooded hills at the southeast of Oz, the black-water lake, and the supposed Crinklink. The Wizard says that traveling alone through this fairy country can be dangerous.

l: Emerald City, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: Dorothy and Toto live in the Emerald City of Oz but sometimes leave it to travel through the country. After the Wizard's trick, Dorothy decides to go back there with Toto.

l: the wild wooded hills at the southeast of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: The wild wooded hills at the southeast of Oz are usually avoided by travelers because many magical things abound there. Dorothy and Toto enter the hills, cross them with the supposed Crinklink, and reach his log castle.

l: the black-water lake, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: The black-water lake is large and deep, blocking Dorothy and Toto's path because there is no bridge or boat. The tiny ferryman claims he can carry them across it, and the disguised Wizard crosses it in one giant step while holding them.

l: the ferryman, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: The ferryman appears as a man no taller than three inches, with blue hair, scarlet clothes, and animal-head buttons on his jacket. He claims that he can carry people across the black-water lake by having them close their eyes and say the word. He is later revealed to have been the Wizard of Oz in disguise.

l: Crinklink's log castle, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: Crinklink's log castle stands on the highest peak of the hills. It contains one large room, a table and chair, a tiny bed, and piles of soiled dishes scattered across the floor, corners, and shelves.

l: the dishes, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: The dishes in Crinklink's log castle are all soiled and have been left unwashed for years. Dorothy is ordered to clean them, and a heap of them falls and breaks when Toto attacks the sleeping disguised Wizard.

l: washing the dishes, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: Washing the dishes is the task Crinklink assigns to Dorothy as a supposed captive. Dorothy performs it cautiously for hours without breaking anything, while Crinklink grows sleepy; the task ends when Toto knocks the dishes down during his attack.

l: the Wizard's lesson about traveling alone, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, LITTLE DOROTHY AND TOTO
s: The Wizard's lesson is that it is dangerous for a little girl to wander alone in a fairy country. He creates the false ferryman and Crinklink and makes Dorothy believe she has been captured, hoping to teach her to be more careful.

l: Little Wizard Stories of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, TIKTOK AND THE NOME KING
s: Tiktok visits the Nome King to request new springs and a cog-wheel for his thought and speech machinery. When Tiktok insults the Nome King, the angry King smashes him into scattered pieces with a mace. Kaliko repairs Tiktok, who then frightens the King by appearing to be a phantom. The Nome King apologizes by giving Kaliko a raise and sending Tiktok back to the Land of Oz with jewels for Princess Ozma of Oz.

l: Nome King, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, TIKTOK AND THE NOME KING
s: The Nome King angrily smashes Tiktok with his mace, then becomes ashamed and fears that Princess Ozma of Oz will retaliate. After Kaliko repairs Tiktok, the King mistakes him for a phantom, panics, and finally promises Tiktok jewels for Princess Ozma of Oz.

l: Tiktok the Clockwork Man, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, TIKTOK AND THE NOME KING
s: Tiktok visits the Nome King to request new steel springs for his thought works and a cog-wheel for his speech producer. After being smashed into pieces, he is repaired by Kaliko and returns to normal, though his speech works initially sound gruff. He tells the Nome King that he is real, not a phantom, and prepares to return to the Land of Oz with jewels.

l: Kaliko, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, TIKTOK AND THE NOME KING
s: Kaliko, the Nome King's Chief Steward, repairs Tiktok by fitting his scattered pieces together and making replacements for worn or imperfect parts. He later explains to the Nome King that Tiktok is real and asks forgiveness for repairing him. The Nome King forgives Kaliko and raises his wages.

l: Princess Ozma, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, TIKTOK AND THE NOME KING
s: Princess Ozma of Oz is Tiktok's powerful ruler and favorite, and the Nome King fears that she will be angry when he destroys Tiktok. The King expects her to send an army against him, but instead resolves to send Tiktok back to her with jewels.

l: Tiktok's destruction, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, TIKTOK AND THE NOME KING
s: Tiktok's destruction occurs when the Nome King hurls his heavy mace at him, bursting the bolts that hold his metal body together. His wheels, pins, cogs, and springs scatter across the floor, leaving only a scrap-heap.

l: Tiktok's repair, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, TIKTOK AND THE NOME KING
s: Tiktok's repair is completed by Kaliko over two weeks of steady work. Kaliko fits the pieces together, replaces worn or imperfect parts, and restores Tiktok's motion, thought, and speech machinery.

l: the Nome King's anger, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, TIKTOK AND THE NOME KING
s: The Nome King's anger is caused partly by a painful bitten tongue and later by Tiktok's insulting remarks. It leads him to destroy Tiktok, an act he regrets and recognizes as a result of his unreasoning temper. He resolves never to become angry again unless something annoys him.

l: Little Wizard Stories of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: Princess Ozma and the Wizard of Oz travel from the Emerald City through the Land of Oz to learn whether its people are happy and to correct any wrongs. In a valley in the mountains, they meet three mischievous Imps who torment travelers and a nearby family. The Wizard successively transforms the Imps into thorny bushes, white pigs, blue doves, and finally three buttons containing their spirits. Ozma and the Wizard plan to keep the buttons until the Imps repent and can be restored as good citizens.

l: Princess Ozma, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: Princess Ozma rules the Land of Oz and wants all its people to be happy, so she travels with the Wizard of Oz to investigate complaints. She confronts the three mischievous Imps, orders the Wizard to use magic against them, and later agrees that keeping their spirits in buttons may reform them.

l: Wizard of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: The Wizard of Oz accompanies Princess Ozma on her journey and brings his bag of magic tools. He transforms the Imps several times, dries his clothes after being thrown into the river, and finally places their spirits in three buttons so they can repent.

l: Emerald City, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: The Emerald City is the beautiful city at the center of the Land of Oz, where Princess Ozma rules and the Wizard of Oz lives in a cozy suite of rooms in the palace.

l: Land of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: The Land of Oz is ruled by Princess Ozma, who wants its inhabitants to be happy and contented. Ozma and the Wizard travel through it seeking problems that should be corrected.

l: Ozma and the Wizard's journey through the Land of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: Ozma and the Wizard leave the Emerald City and wander through the country for many days, eventually reaching a mountainous place neither has visited before. Their journey leads them to a valley where they try to protect travelers from three mischievous Imps.

l: valley in the mountains, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: The valley lies beyond a rocky path and contains three caves where the Imps live. The Imps harass travelers and a family in a nearby cottage, so Ozma and the Wizard enter the valley to find them.

l: three mischievous Imps, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: The three Imps are small, lively creatures with big round ears, flat noses, wide grinning mouths, and black hair shaped like horns. They jeer at travelers, call them names, push them, throw stones, and later attack Ozma and the Wizard even after being transformed.

l: Imp Olite, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: Imp Olite is one of the three mischievous Imps who torment travelers and attack Princess Ozma and the Wizard of Oz. After several transformations, Olite's spirit is contained in a tin button.

l: Imp Udent, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: Imp Udent is one of the three mischievous Imps who torment travelers and attack Princess Ozma and the Wizard of Oz. After several transformations, Udent's spirit is contained in a brass button.

l: Imp Ertinent, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: Imp Ertinent is one of the three mischievous Imps who torment travelers and attack Princess Ozma and the Wizard of Oz. After several transformations, Ertinent's spirit is contained in a lead button.

l: thorny bushes transformed from the Imps, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: The Wizard first transforms the three Imps into thorny, stubby bushes rooted in the ground. The bushes soon move across the earth and prick the Wizard while trying to injure Ozma, so he transforms them again.

l: white pigs transformed from the Imps, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: The Wizard accidentally transforms the thorny bushes into three fat, roly-poly white pigs instead of mice. The pigs continue the Imps' mischief by tripping Ozma and the Wizard and pushing the Wizard into the river.

l: blue doves transformed from the Imps, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: The Wizard transforms the white pigs into three blue doves, believing doves are harmless. The doves instead attack Ozma and the Wizard by pecking at their eyes, biting the Wizard's fingers, and tweaking Ozma's ear.

l: three buttons containing the Imps' spirits, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: The Wizard transforms the blue doves into a tin button for Imp Olite, a brass button for Imp Udent, and a lead button for Imp Ertinent. He places the buttons in a box and plans to sew them onto his coat until the Imps repent; then the buttons will become silver, gold, and aluminum and the Imps can be restored to good forms.

l: magic, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, OZMA AND THE LITTLE WIZARD
s: The Wizard uses magic to transform the Imps from living creatures into bushes, pigs, doves, and finally buttons. His magic also dries his clothes after the river incident, and he explains that the Imps' spirits can change the buttons when they repent.

l: Little Wizard Stories of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, JACK PUMPKINHEAD AND THE SAWHORSE
s: Ozma sees through the Magic Picture that a little girl and a little boy are lost in a western forest, so she sends Jack Pumpkinhead to rescue them. Jack rides the Sawhorse to the forest, finds the children bound by the King of all the Squirrels, and frees them after learning they took nuts because they were hungry. A falling limb smashes Jack's pumpkin head, leaving him helpless, but the Sawhorse carries him and the children until the little Wizard arrives. The little Wizard returns the children to their friends and gives Jack a new pumpkin head at his home.

l: Princess Ozma, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, JACK PUMPKINHEAD AND THE SAWHORSE
s: Ozma sees the lost little girl and little boy in the Magic Picture and sends Jack Pumpkinhead to rescue them. After Jack's head is smashed, she sends the little Wizard mounted on the Cowardly Lion to save Jack and the children.

l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, JACK PUMPKINHEAD AND THE SAWHORSE
s: Jack Pumpkinhead travels on the Sawhorse to rescue two lost children in the western forest. He frees them from the squirrels, but a falling limb smashes his pumpkin head; the little Wizard later gives him a new head.

l: Sawhorse, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, JACK PUMPKINHEAD AND THE SAWHORSE
s: The Sawhorse carries Jack Pumpkinhead to the forest and later carries Jack's headless body and the two children away from the squirrels. It becomes lost among the branching paths until the Cowardly Lion leads it out, and it then carries Jack to his home for restoration.

l: Wizard of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz, JACK PUMPKINHEAD AND THE SAWHORSE
s: The little Wizard rides the Cowardly Lion to the forest after Ozma sends him to rescue Jack and the children. He brings the children back to their friends, takes Jack to his pumpkin field, and gives him a new pumpkin head.
